problem: In Spanish 'el gato' is masculine, while the Arabic translation uses the feminine 'القطّة'. Both are fine, just a minor gender mismatch.
fix: طارد الكلب القطّ في أنحاء الحديقة كلها حتى تسلّق القطّ شجرة.

problem: Semantically unnatural in all three languages: not drinking water soon doesn't make the speaker freeze it ('la vas a congelar'); it would make more sense as 'se va a congelar' (it will freeze) or using another food item.
fix: Si no usas estas verduras pronto, tendrás que congelarlas para que no se estropeen.

problem: In Spanish, 'negar que' requires the subjunctive mood ('rompiera' or 'haya roto'), or the infinitive ('haber roto') when the subject is the same. Using the indicative 'rompió' is ungrammatical.
fix: Él niega haber roto la ventana.

problem: In Spanish, 'negar que' requires the subjunctive mood ('hubiera robado'), or the infinitive ('haber robado') when the subject is the same. Using the indicative 'había robado' is ungrammatical.
fix: El hombre negó haber robado el dinero, pero la cámara mostró la verdad.

problem: The Arabic translation says 'will start after a week' (ستبدأ بعد أسبوع) instead of 'will start a week later' (una semana más tarde).
fix: أعلنت المدرسة أمس أن الدروس ستبدأ متأخرة بأسبوع.

problem: In the Arabic translation, 'تُعجب' (she likes/admires) is used instead of 'تُثير إعجاب' or 'تُبهر' (she impresses).
fix: ar: أعدّت عرضها بعناية كبيرة لأنها أرادت أن تُبهر مديرها الجديد.

problem: 'sabe obedecer' (knows how to obey) sounds somewhat unnatural; 'El perro es muy listo y siempre obedece a la niña...' is much more natural.
fix: El perro es muy listo y siempre obedece a la niña pequeña de la casa.

problem: In Spanish, 'Lavarse las manos' (reflexive) is the standard, natural phrasing rather than 'Lavar las manos'.
fix: Lavarse las manos ayuda a prevenir enfermedades.

problem: Plural noun 'dibujos animados' is given the singular article 'el' instead of 'los'.
fix: details: gender=m; article=los

problem: With indefinite 'Todo ciudadano que...', the subjunctive 'tenga' is much more natural in Spanish than the indicative 'tiene'.
fix: Todo ciudadano que tenga más de dieciocho años puede votar para elegir al nuevo alcalde.

problem: In Peninsular Spanish (Spain), 'caliente' is unnatural when describing climate or weather; 'cálido' or 'caluroso' is standard.
fix: El clima aquí es seco y caluroso.

problem: In Peninsular Spanish (Spain), 'caliente' is unnatural when describing climate; 'cálido' or 'caluroso' is used instead.
fix: El clima de esta zona es seco y caluroso, así que la gente tiene muchos olivos.

problem: 'donde un médico viene' is slightly awkward; 'a la que viene un médico' is more natural with a verb of motion.
fix: En el pueblo hay una clínica pequeña a la que viene un médico dos veces por semana.

problem: The term 'datos' is masculine plural, so the article in details should be 'los', not singular 'el'.
fix: details: gender=m; article=los

problem: Using 'mi empresario' to mean 'my boss/employer' in everyday speech is unnatural in Spanish; native speakers say 'mi jefe' or 'mi empresa'. 'Empresario' is used as a formal/legal term for employers in general or to mean 'businessman/entrepreneur'.
'agua caliente' means 'hot water', whereas the English and Arabic translations say 'warm water' (which would be 'agua tibia' or 'agua templada').
fix: Para hacer el pan, mezcla la harina con agua tibia y un poco de sal.

problem: In Arabic, 'el centro' (downtown/city centre) is more naturally translated as 'وسط المدينة' rather than just 'الوسط'.
fix: زرنا معرضًا فنّيًا في وسط المدينة.

problem: 'El gato' is masculine in Spanish, whereas the Arabic translation uses the feminine 'القطّة'. Using 'القطّ' is more accurate.
fix: خرج القطّ من فجوة تحت باب الحديقة وذهب إلى الشارع.

problem: In Arabic, 'قواعدي' (my rules) sounds unnatural for 'my grammar' and 'ما زالت ليست' is clunky.
fix: ar: أفهم تقريبًا كل ما يقوله الناس، لكن قواعد اللغة عندي ليست جيدة جدًّا بعد.

problem: In Peninsular Spanish, 'Llévate la sudadera' or 'Ponte la sudadera' is much more natural than 'Lleva la sudadera' as an imperative to take/wear clothing.
fix: Llévate la sudadera, hace frío.

problem: The Arabic meaning only includes 'trainer' (حذاء رياضي) and omits 'slipper' (خفّ / شبشب), even though example 2 uses the 'slipper' meaning.
fix: ar: حذاء رياضي، خفّ

problem: In English, 'broken' is unnatural for shoes ('worn out' or 'torn' is natural); in Arabic, 'مكسور' (broken) is unnatural for shoes ('ممزق' or 'تالف' is natural).
fix: en: My running shoes are worn out. | ar: حذائي الرياضي ممزق.

problem: In Spanish, washing one's own hands requires the reflexive verb 'lavarse' ('Hay que lavarse las manos con agua y jabón').
fix: Hay que lavarse las manos con agua y jabón.

problem: 'pasta de dientes' is feminine, not masculine.
fix: gender=f; article=la

problem: 'tijeras' is plural, so the article should be 'las' (or the term should be 'tijera').
fix: gender=f; article=las

problem: Grammatical error in Spanish: 'y' must change to 'e' before words starting with the 'i' sound ('e intentó').
fix: Un zorro entró anoche en el jardín e intentó coger una de nuestras gallinas.

problem: Singular feminine nouns starting with stressed 'a' take the masculine singular article 'el' ('el ala'), not 'la'.
fix: article=el

problem: 'ser igual con los dos' is unnatural in Spanish to mean 'treat both equally' (usually 'tratar por igual a los dos' or 'ser justo con los dos').
fix: Los dos hermanos recibieron la misma cantidad de dinero, porque su padre quería tratarlos por igual a los dos.

problem: Ungrammatical Spanish: 'cualquier' cannot be used in the scope of 'no' like English 'anywhere'; negative clauses require 'ningún' ('no las encuentro en ningún sitio'). Use 'en cualquier sitio' in an affirmative or conditional clause instead.
fix: Si dejas las llaves en cualquier sitio, luego no las vas a encontrar.

problem: Spanish has plural 'mis redacciones... dárselas' (my essays... give them), whereas the Arabic translation uses singular ('إنشائي... أسلّمه').
fix: تساعدني أختي في تحرير مواضيع التعبير الخاصة بي قبل أن أسلّمها إلى المعلّمة.

problem: In Peninsular Spanish, 'no vaciles' commonly means 'don't mess with me / don't joke around'. For 'don't hesitate', 'no dudes en llamar' is much more natural.
fix: No vaciles en llamar si necesitas ayuda.

problem: In Spanish, 'proceder a + physical location' (in the sense of 'go/walk to') is an anglicism; 'proceder a' is normally used with actions/infinitives or event nouns (e.g., 'proceder a la evacuación'). In Spain, 'dirigirse a la salida' is standard.
fix: Por favor, vamos a proceder a la votación.

problem: Using 'proceder a' to mean 'go/walk to a physical place' (gate 12) is an anglicism in Spanish; 'dirigirse a' is standard in Spain, while 'proceder a' is used with actions (e.g., 'proceder al embarque').
fix: Los pasajeros del vuelo a Roma ya pueden proceder al embarque en la puerta número doce.

problem: In Spanish, resisting temptation usually uses the pronominal form 'resistirse a' (No pude resistirme al chocolate) or 'resistir la tentación'. 'Resistir el chocolate' sounds like enduring it.
fix: No pude resistirme al chocolate.

problem: Similar to ex1, 'resistir el pastel' is unnatural in Spanish for resisting temptation; it should be 'resistirme al pastel' or 'resistir la tentación del pastel'.
fix: Quise resistirme al pastel de chocolate, pero al final me comí dos trozos grandes.

problem: In Arabic, 'كل بعد ظهر هذا الأسبوع' is an awkward literal translation of 'every afternoon this week'.
fix: ar: سيتدرّب الفريق بعد ظهر كل يوم من هذا الأسبوع قبل المباراة النهائية.

problem: In Arabic, حرفة (craft/occupation) normally refers to the skill or profession, not physical items sold; مشغولات يدوية or منتجات حرفية is more natural for 'sell crafts'.
fix: يبيعون في السوق مشغولات يدوية محلية.

problem: In Arabic, حرفًا means professions/trades rather than physical craft items; مشغولات يدوية محلية or صناعات حرفية محلية is more accurate.
fix: يبيع السوق مشغولات يدوية محلية، كالسلال والصحون والبطّانيات المصنوعة يدويًّا.

problem: In Spanish, feminine nouns beginning with stressed 'a-' or 'ha-' take the singular definite article 'el' (el águila), not 'la'. Also, in formal Arabic ' eagle' is عقاب while نسر is vulture, though نسر is widely used colloquially.
fix: details: gender=f; article=el

problem: Singular 'elección' usually means 'choice', while 'election' is almost always plural ('elecciones') in Spain, and the Arabic translation انتخابات is plural.
fix: meaning: en: election, choice | ar: انتخاب، اختيار

problem: In Peninsular Spanish, 'poner una multa' is standard and natural; 'dar una multa' sounds like an anglicism ('give a fine').
fix: La policía me puso una multa ayer.

problem: In Spanish, parts of the body normally take the definite article with an indirect object pronoun ('tócale la frente') rather than a possessive ('toca su frente').
fix: Tiene fiebre, tócale la frente.

problem: In Spanish, the adjective 'sano' (masculine) agrees with 'el bebé', whereas the English and Arabic translations refer to a female baby ('she' / 'الطفلة'). In Spanish, if referring specifically to a female baby with an adjective, 'sana' or 'la bebé' would typically be used, though 'el bebé... sano' can be generic.
fix: en: The doctor checks the baby's growth every month to see that he's healthy. | ar: يتابع الطبيب نموّ الرضيع كل شهر ليتأكّد من أنه بصحّة جيدة.

problem: Ungrammatical Spanish: 'te pueden doler el estómago'. The subject of 'doler' is singular ('el estómago'), so the verb must be singular ('te puede doler el estómago'), or a causative verb like 'dar' should be used with 'los plátanos' as the subject.
fix: No comas esos plátanos todavía, porque no están maduros y te puede doler el estómago.

problem: In Arabic, 'أصلية' usually means 'authentic/original (not a copy)'. In the context of an idea ('una idea original'), 'مبتكرة' or 'فريدة' (creative/unique) is much more natural.
fix: إنّها فكرة مبتكرة جدًا.

problem: In Spanish, 'una semana muy pacífica' sounds unnatural (a week isn't non-violent); native speakers would say 'una semana muy tranquila' or 'apacible'.
fix: El pueblo donde pasamos las vacaciones era un lugar muy pacífico donde solo se oían los pájaros.

problem: In the Arabic translation, 'ضجيجًا' should be in the nominative case ('ضجيجٌ') as it is the delayed subject (مبتدأ مؤخر), not governed by 'لكن' (which already has the attached pronoun 'ها' as its ism).
fix: في المناطق الحضرية فرص عمل أكثر، لكن فيها أيضًا ضجيجٌ أكثر ومساحة أقلّ.

problem: In Arabic, 'طبق نموذجي' means 'model/exemplary dish'; for food from a region ('plato típico'), 'طبق تقليدي' (traditional) or 'طبق شعبي' is much more natural.
fix: ar: إنّه طبق تقليدي من بلدي.

problem: In Arabic, 'طبق نموذجي' means 'model/exemplary dish'; for regional food ('plato típico'), 'طبق تقليدي' or 'طبق شعبي' is much more natural.
fix: ar: الباييا طبق تقليدي في هذه المنطقة، ويأكلها الناس في أيام الأحد.

problem: The Arabic 'أنا موافق معك' is a literal calque; 'أنا متفق معك تمامًا' or 'أوافقك تمامًا' is much more natural in MSA.
fix: أنا متفق معك تمامًا.

problem: 'plantas' means 'plants', whereas English translates it as 'weeds' and Arabic as 'wild plants' (نباتات برية). In Spanish, weeds would be 'malas hierbas' or 'maleza'.
fix: Nadie vivía en la casa desde hacía años, y el jardín estaba muy descuidado y lleno de malas hierbas.

problem: In Spain, 'pulir' is used for metals, stone, wood, or fingernails, not typically for shoes (which uses 'limpiar' or 'sacar brillo a').
In Spain, 'pulir zapatos' sounds like a calque from English 'polish shoes'; 'sacar brillo a' or 'lustrar' is standard for footwear.
In Spanish, sucking one's own finger/thumb is idiomatic with the reflexive verb and definite article ('se chupa el dedo'), whereas 'chupa su dedo' sounds unnatural.
fix: El bebé se chupa el dedo.

problem: In Spanish, 'chuparse el dedo' requires the reflexive pronoun ('chuparse'), and 'está cansado' is masculine while the Arabic translation uses feminine ('الطفلة / تتعب').
fix: Al bebé le gusta chuparse el dedo cuando está cansado y quiere dormir un poco. | ar: يحبّ الطفل أن يمصّ إصبعه حين يتعب ويريد أن ينام قليلًا.

problem: The Arabic verb يطلّق (yutalliq) is transitive ('to divorce someone'), whereas divorciarse is reflexive/intransitive ('to get divorced', يتطلّق or ينفصل).
fix: ar: يتطلّق

problem: 'nombrar [algo] con el nombre de [alguien]' is unnatural and redundant in Spanish (unlike English 'to name after'); in Spanish one says 'ponerle a la plaza el nombre de...' or 'bautizar la plaza con el nombre de...'.
'Provocar una alarma' sounds unnatural for setting off a physical alarm (usually 'activar' or 'hacer saltar'); 'provocar alarma' without the article means to cause public alarm/panic.
fix: El humo provocó un incendio.

problem: 'Provocar la alarma' is unnatural in Spanish for triggering a fire alarm device ('hacer saltar la alarma' or 'activar la alarma' is standard).
fix: Un pequeño fuego en la cocina provocó mucho humo, y todos tuvieron que salir del edificio.

problem: In Spanish, 'revisar que' expressing a purpose/verification to ensure something is the case typically takes the subjunctive ('revisa bien que no haya errores').
fix: Antes de enviar el correo, revisa bien que no haya errores en los nombres ni en las fechas.

problem: Singular definite article for 'ave' is 'el' because it starts with a stressed 'a-' (even though the noun is feminine).
fix: gender=f; article=el

problem: In Arabic, águila (eagle) is عقاب, whereas نسر means vulture (buitre), though نسر is widely misused for eagle in everyday Arabic.
fix: العقاب طائر كبير جدًا.

problem: The Arabic translation omits 'con la comida' (with the meal).
fix: ar: أيّ مشروب تريد مع الطعام؟

problem: In Arabic, 'cuna' (cot/crib) is translated as 'سريره' (his bed) instead of 'مهده' (his cot/cradle).

problem: English lists both 'plug, socket', and both examples use the 'socket' sense (مقبس), while the Arabic definition only lists 'قابس' (plug).

problem: In Arabic, 'البطاقة' means card/tag; 'الملصق' (consistent with the word entry and ex1) is more natural for a bottle label.

problem: In Arabic, 'معرض' means exhibition/trade fair; a funfair with rides in a village is better translated as 'مهرجان' or 'ملاهي'.
fix: كل سبتمبر يُقام في القرية مهرجان فيه ألعاب وموسيقى وطعام تقليدي.

problem: In Spanish, 'Lleva una gorra' is normally understood as the 3rd person indicative ('He/She is wearing a cap'), whereas the imperative 'Wear a cap' would naturally be 'Ponte una gorra'.
fix: Ponte una gorra por el sol.

problem: Saying 'los dos lados' for the two sides of a legal case is an anglicism; 'las dos partes' or 'ambas partes' is natural in Spanish.
fix: El juez escuchó a las dos partes.

problem: The Arabic translation means 'This is a lie' and omits 'Lo que dice ese hombre' ('What that man says').
fix: ما يقوله ذلك الرجل كذب.

problem: 'bolsa de cristal' literally means 'glass bag', which makes no sense and does not mean 'glass bowl' / 'حوض زجاجي'. Use 'pecera de cristal' or 'cuenco de cristal'.
fix: Mi hija tiene un pez naranja en una pecera de cristal y le da de comer cada mañana.

problem: In Spanish, 'llevar' means to wear (already have on) or to carry, not 'to put on' as a command before bed. It should be 'ponte el pijama'.
fix: Ya es tarde, ponte el pijama. ¦ meaning: en: It's late now, put on your pyjamas. | ar: الوقت متأخّر الآن، البس البيجامة.

problem: 'سقط برق' in Arabic sounds unnatural for a lightning strike; 'ضربت صاعقة' is much more idiomatic.
fix: ضربت صاعقة الشجرة.

problem: The Arabic translation omits the word 'frío' (باردًا - cold).
fix: هل تريد مشروبًا غازيًا باردًا؟

problem: In the Arabic translation, 'بأحد يومين' is slightly awkward without 'لمدة' (for two days), and 'إشارة' is closer to the target word than 'تغطية'.
fix: لا توجد إشارة للهاتف المحمول في الجبال، لذلك لم نستطع أن نتّصل بأحد لمدة يومين.

problem: In standard Arabic, 'my father-in-law' is 'حماي' (as in ex1) or 'حمي', whereas 'حموي' is non-standard.
fix: يعمل حماي في الحقول كل يوم، مع أنه قارب الثمانين.

problem: The Arabic translation 'يا لك من أخفتني!' is ungrammatical.
fix: ar: كم أخفتني! / لقد أرعبتني!

problem: In Spanish, clothing size is usually 'la talla', whereas 'el tamaño' refers to general physical dimensions.
In Arabic, 'سقف' usually means ceiling (techo), whereas roof (tejado) is more accurately 'سطح' or 'سقف خارجي / قرميد'.
fix: ar: سطح / سقف خارجي

problem: In Arabic, 'على السقف' sounds like 'on the ceiling'; 'على السطح' is more natural for 'on the roof'.
fix: ar: هناك قطّ على السطح.

problem: The Arabic translation omits 'Ahora' (الآن).

problem: In Arabic, 'نفد' is a verb ('it ran out'); as an adjective matching 'agotado', 'نافد' is more accurate.
fix: ar: منهك؛ نافد

problem: In Arabic, using 'قضينا بعد ظهر لطيفًا' (we spent a pleasant after-noon) is grammatically awkward because 'بعد ظهر' is an adverbial phrase, not a standard countable noun for a period of time. 'قضينا وقتًا لطيفًا جدًّا بعد الظهر' or 'قضينا ظهيرة لطيفة جدًّا' is much more natural.
fix: ar: قضينا ظهيرة لطيفة جدًّا مع الجيران الجدد، وتحدّثنا حتى وقت متأخّر جدًّا.

problem: With 'ser' and a person (especially service staff), 'atento' means 'courteous / helpful / considerate' rather than 'paying attention' (which would use 'estar'). In Arabic, 'منتبه' means 'alert / paying attention', whereas a courteous/attentive waiter is 'خدوم' or 'مهذّب' or 'لطيف'.
fix: ar: النادل خدوم جدًا.

problem: In Spanish, 'estar atento en clase' is much more natural than 'ser atento en clase' when meaning 'to pay attention in class' ('ser atento' usually means 'to be polite/considerate').
fix: El alumno nuevo está muy atento en clase y siempre hace preguntas interesantes.

problem: The Arabic literal translation 'مع المفاتيح' (with the keys) sounds unnatural after 'شارد الذهن'; 'فيما يخص المفاتيح' or 'أنسى المفاتيح كثيرًا' would be much more natural.
fix: ar: أنا كثير النسيان للمفاتيح.

problem: The Arabic translation is missing the first part of the sentence ('Espera aquí' / 'Wait here').
fix: ar: انتظر هنا، سأعود فورًا.

problem: The Arabic translation omits 'otra vez' ('again').
fix: ar: على الأرجح سيصل متأخّرًا مرة أخرى.

problem: 'El coche se rompió' is somewhat unnatural in Spain for 'the car broke down' ('se estropeó' or 'se averió' is much more idiomatic).
fix: El coche se estropeó en la carretera, pero afortunadamente un hombre amable nos ayudó.

problem: In Arabic, 'أدركت رائحة' is slightly unnatural for perceiving a smell; 'شممت' or 'شعرت برائحة' or 'لاحظت رائحة' is much more natural.
fix: ar: لاحظت رائحة غريبة في المطبخ.

problem: In Spain, 'la entrada al museo' is standard for a ticket/entry fee; 'admisión' sounds like an Anglicism here ( usually used for university/club acceptance or 'derecho de admisión').

problem: Same as ex1: in Spain, 'la entrada al museo' is used for museum entry rather than 'la admisión'.
In Spanish, 'hacha' is feminine, but because it starts with a stressed /a/ sound, it takes the singular definite article 'el' ('el hacha'), not 'la'.

problem: In Spanish, a visitor's ID badge is typically called 'acreditación', 'identificación', or 'credencial'. 'Insignia' usually refers to a military/police badge, emblem, or pin.
In Spanish, a visitor's name badge is called 'acreditación', 'identificación', or 'credencial', rather than 'insignia' (which means emblem/pin/police badge).
In Spanish, 'fardo' refers to a large bale or bundle (e.g., of hay, cloth, or merchandise); for letters tied with a ribbon, 'fajo' or 'atado' is the natural word.
Putting 'de la tabla' after 'en la otra' sounds slightly awkward in Spanish compared to putting it after 'en una columna'.
fix: Los alumnos escribieron sus nombres en una columna de la tabla y sus notas en la otra.

problem: The word 'cometa' is masculine when meaning 'comet' (el cometa) and feminine when meaning 'kite' (la cometa), but details only list masculine (el).
fix: gender=m/f; article=el/la

problem: The Arabic translation uses singular for both 'shoes' and 'laces' ('لحذائي رباط أحمر'), while the Spanish and English use plural ('Mis zapatos tienen cordones rojos' / 'My shoes have red laces').
fix: لحذائي أربطة حمراء.

problem: In Spain, a school counsellor is called 'orientador', not 'consejero del colegio' (which is a calque from English).
In Spain, a school counsellor is called 'orientador', not 'consejero del colegio' (which is a calque from English).
In English, 'on the plate' is more natural than 'in the plate'.
fix: My son only eats the middle of the sandwich and always leaves the crust on the plate.

problem: The term 'cubiertos' is plural, so the article in details should be 'los', not 'el'.
fix: gender=m; article=los

problem: The term 'lácteos' is plural, so the article in details should be 'los', not 'el'.
fix: gender=m; article=los

problem: In Arabic, translating 'yogur' as 'اللبن' alongside 'الحليب' can be ambiguous depending on the dialect; 'الزبادي' is clearer in MSA.
fix: قال لها الطبيب أن تكثر من منتجات الألبان، كالحليب والزبادي، لتبقى عظامها قوية.

problem: In Arabic, 'أيل' is more accurate for 'ciervo' (deer), while 'غزال' is 'gacela' (gazelle), though 'غزال' is widely used colloquially.
fix: أيل / غزال

problem: The term 'pinzas' is plural, but the article in details is singular ('la' instead of 'las').
fix: details: gender=f; article=las

problem: In Spanish, 'me la pusiera' (with the reflexive pronoun 'me') is much more natural than 'la pusiera' when referring to applying ointment to oneself.
fix: El médico me dio una pomada para la piel y me dijo que me la pusiera dos veces al día.

problem: The Arabic translation 'القلعة أطلال' (The castle is ruins) sounds slightly unnatural compared to 'القلعة في حالة خراب' or 'القلعة متهدّمة'.
fix: القلعة في حالة خراب.

problem: In Arabic, 'لذلك' usually reads as 'therefore'. Using 'يمتلك ذلك الرجل الغني يختًا' or 'لدى ذلك الرجل الغني يخت' avoids this ambiguity.
fix: ar: لدى ذلك الرجل الغني يخت.

problem: In Spanish, 'oído' (inner ear) is used for hearing sounds inside the ear, rather than 'oreja' (outer ear), and possessive adjectives are normally replaced by definite articles with body parts.
fix: Tengo un zumbido en el oído.

problem: Arabic 'كسول' means 'lazy' (perezoso), whereas 'ocioso' means 'idle / unoccupied' (عاطل / خامل).
fix: ar: خامل، عاطل

problem: In Arabic, فضفاض means 'loose-fitting' (as in baggy clothes), whereas Spanish 'suelto' means 'unfastened, untied, loose' (as shown in the examples with hair and a bicycle wheel). 'منفكّ' or 'مرتخٍ' fits better.
fix: ar: منفكّ / مرتخٍ

problem: The Spanish clause 'tan pegajosas que lo tocaban todo' means 'so sticky that they touched everything', which makes little logical sense as a consequence and does not match the English/Arabic translations ('got everything sticky' / 'لطّخوا بها كل شيء').
fix: Después de comer el pastel de miel, los niños tenían las manos tan pegajosas que lo manchaban todo.

problem: The term field contains the POS tag 'adj' ('desierto adj') instead of just the word.
fix: term: desierto ¦ reading:  ¦ part_of_speech: adj ¦ meaning: en: deserted | ar: مهجور

problem: In Spanish, 'estar' with an indefinite subject ('Una mariquita está en la hoja') sounds unnatural; existential 'Hay una mariquita en la hoja' is normally used.
fix: Hay una mariquita en la hoja.

problem: Missing diaeresis in Spanish spelling: 'pinguino' should be 'pingüino'.
fix: pingüino

problem: Missing personal 'a' before a definite animate object ('vimos a los pingüinos'), or better phrased without 'que' ('vimos a los pingüinos nadando').
fix: En el zoo vimos a los pingüinos nadando muy rápido en el agua fría.

problem: In Arabic, 'المفتاح' alone usually means 'key'; 'مفتاح الكهرباء' is clearer for 'switch'.
fix: ar: مفتاح الكهرباء بجانب الباب.

problem: The term 'espinacas' is plural, so the article in details should be 'las' (or the term should be singular 'espinaca' with 'la').
fix: details: gender=f; article=las

problem: Writing dictation in textbooks ('libros') is odd; 'cuadernos' (notebooks) is much more natural.
fix: La profesora empezó a dictar la lección despacio, y los alumnos la escribían en sus cuadernos.

problem: 'que lo fuera a exhalar' is unnatural in Spanish (sounds like an awkward avoidance of conjugating the subjunctive); 'que lo exhalara' or 'después de tomar aire... exhalarlo despacio' is much more natural.
fix: El médico me dijo que tomara aire por la nariz y que luego lo exhalara despacio por la boca.

problem: In Spanish, 'pedir + infinitive' when the subjects are different ('me pidió inhalar') is awkward; normally 'me pidió que inhalara' is used.
fix: El médico me pidió que inhalara muy hondo mientras me ponía la mano en el pecho con cuidado.

problem: In Arabic, 'يسدّ' (blocks) is much more natural than 'يعرقل' (hinders) for a physical obstacle like a fallen tree.
fix: شجرة ساقطة تسدّ الطريق.

problem: 'abrumar' has a negative/stressful connotation (weigh down, overburden), whereas Arabic 'يغمر' is usually neutral or positive (flood with joy/love). 'يرهق' or 'يثقل كاهل' is more accurate.
fix: يرهق، يثقل كاهل

problem: In Arabic, 'العمل يغمرني' sounds somewhat unnatural; 'العمل يرهقني' or 'يثقل كاهلي' fits the meaning of 'abruma' much better.
fix: العمل يرهقني هذا الأسبوع.

problem: In Arabic, يخشخش means 'to rustle' (like dry leaves or paper); for a rattling train, يقرقع or يقعقع is more accurate.
fix: ar: كان القطار القديم يقرقع عبر الريف.

problem: Using the infinitive 'abstenerse' as a direct polite request after 'Por favor' is grammatically proscribed in Spanish (unless it is an impersonal sign); 'absténganse' or 'se ruega abstenerse' is standard.
fix: Por favor, se ruega abstenerse de usar el móvil durante la obra de teatro para no molestar a los actores.

problem: Using 'pudo sobresaltar' to keep the infinitive is unnatural in Spanish here, and 'pudo' is omitted in the translations.
fix: El ruido de la puerta al cerrarse con el viento llegó a sobresaltar a toda la familia.

problem: The word 'escombros' is plural, so the article should be 'los', not 'el'.
fix: details: gender=m; article=los

problem: 'Tener fatiga' in Spain often means 'to feel nauseous/sick' rather than 'to be tired' (normally 'estar fatigado/cansado' or 'sentir fatiga').
fix: Después del viaje sentía mucha fatiga.

problem: In Arabic, 'برد' without diacritics is ambiguous with 'بَرْد' (cold). Adding fatha on the second letter 'بَرَد' makes it unambiguously 'hail'.
fix: ar: بَرَد

problem: In Spanish, animate direct objects usually require the personal 'a' (tuvo a un rehén), and 'retuvo' or 'mantuvo' is much more natural than 'tuvo' for 'held a hostage'.
fix: El hombre retuvo a un rehén durante dos días.

problem: The word 'celos' is masculine plural, so the article must be 'los', not 'el'.
fix: gender=m; article=los

problem: 'Un farol viejo está en la calle oscura' is unnatural in Spanish because indefinite subjects normally use 'hay' instead of 'estar'.Also in Spain 'farola' is much more common for streetlamp.
fix: Hay un farol viejo en la calle oscura.

problem: The Arabic phrase 'يقومون بالشقاوة' is unnatural.
fix: الأطفال يقومون بأفعال شغب دائمًا.

problem: In Arabic, 'ضريح' refers specifically to a mausoleum or tomb. 'مزار' (shrine) or 'حرم / ملاذ' (sanctuary) is more accurate for 'santuario'.
fix: ar: مزار، ملاذ

problem: In Spanish, 'me mareo' or 'tengo mareos' is much more natural than 'tengo mareo' (singular).
fix: En el barco siempre me mareo.

problem: 'Tengo mareo' (singular) sounds slightly unnatural; 'me mareo' or 'sufro de mareos' is much more common.
fix: Siempre tengo mareos cuando viajo en barco, así que prefiero ir a la isla en avión.

problem: 'Juega en la puerta' and 'pelotas' are unnatural in Spanish for football; 'juega en la portería' (or 'de portero') and 'balones' are standard.
fix: El chico que juega en la portería es muy ágil y puede parar casi todos los balones.

problem: In Arabic, 'مرتبكًا' means confused/nervous rather than clumsy ('أخرق').
fix: ar: كنت أخرق جدًّا في درس الموسيقى، لأنني لم أعزف أمام أحد قطّ.

problem: Spelling error in the Arabic translation: 'لأكل' should be 'لآكل' (with madda for the 1st person verb 'so I can eat') or 'للأكل' (noun 'for eating').
fix: ar: كان أسبوعًا محمومًا في المكتب، ولم أجد وقتًا حتى لآكل جيدًا.

problem: 'dentado' literally and primarily means 'serrated' or 'toothed'. 'Jagged' is better translated as 'mellado', 'escarpado', or 'irregular'.
fix: en: serrated, jagged

problem: In English, a knife with a 'borde dentado' is called a 'serrated edge', whereas a 'jagged edge' implies it is broken or damaged.
fix: en: The knife has a serrated edge.

problem: Describing beach rocks as 'muy dentadas' in Spanish sounds unnatural (likely a literal translation of English 'jagged rocks'); in Spanish 'escarpadas', 'afiladas', or 'puntiagudas' would be used.
'guiñar' is a completely regular -ar verb (unlike 'roncar' which has a c->qu spelling change). Details has 'irregular=yes'.
fix: details: irregular=no

problem: Repeating 'las patatas' is unnatural in Spanish (especially for L9) and doesn't match the pronouns 'them'/'ها' in the translations.
fix: Pela las patatas y córtalas en trozos.

problem: Minor gender/number agreement issue in Arabic: 'ليصير ألوانه' ('ألوان' is an inanimate plural and takes feminine singular agreement).
fix: تضع أمي البازلاء والجزر في الأرز لتصير ألوانه أكثر ونكهته أغنى.

problem: The term 'prismáticos' is masculine plural, so the article must be 'los', not 'el'.
fix: gender=m; article=los

problem: The term 'alicates' is masculine plural, so the article must be 'los', not 'el' (unless the singular 'alicate' is used).
fix: details: gender=m; article=los | ar: زردية

problem: 'pudo desconcertar' in a 'tan... que' result clause sounds unnatural in Spanish just to keep the infinitive; 'desconcertó' is the natural form matching the translations.
fix: La pregunta del examen era tan rara que desconcertó incluso a los mejores alumnos.

problem: 'erizar(se)' is a regular verb (only standard orthographic c -> z before e, not an irregular conjugation), and Arabic 'ينتصب' alone is overly general compared to 'يقشعرّ / ينتصب الشعر'.
fix: term: erizarse ¦ reading:  ¦ part_of_speech: verb ¦ meaning: en: to bristle | ar: ينتصب الشعر ¦ details: irregular=no

problem: With a person/family as direct object, 'sostener a una familia' (with personal 'a') is much more standard in Spanish.
fix: Es difícil sostener a una familia grande con un solo sueldo cuando todo es tan caro.

problem: 'holgazanear' means 'to laze about / to loaf around' (as used in the examples), rather than 'to dawdle' (which means to move slowly / waste time).
fix: to laze about, to loaf around

problem: The Arabic meaning only includes 'يحلّ' (to disband), missing the primary physical meaning 'يذيب' (to dissolve), which is used in the examples.
fix: ar: يذيب، يحلّ

problem: In Spanish, 'discernir' is usually intellectual/abstract rather than visual ('divisar' or 'distinguir' would be natural for seeing the road in the fog).
Arabic 'يتآكل' is intransitive ('to erode / be corroded', corresponding to 'erosionarse'), whereas 'erosionar' is transitive ('يُعرّي / يؤدّي إلى تآكل').
fix: ar: يُعرّي

problem: The Arabic translation يلتهب means 'to become inflamed' (inflamarse). 'To become infected' is better translated as يُصاب بالعدوى or يتلوّث.
fix: en: to become infected | ar: يُصاب بالعدوى، يلتهب

problem: In English, 'to flaunt' is transitive, whereas 'alardear' is intransitive (alardear de). 'To boast' or 'to show off' is a more accurate match.
fix: en: to boast, to show off | ar: يتباهى

problem: 'Llegó a arrojar' means 'went so far as to fling' or 'ended up flinging', which sounds unnatural here and doesn't match the translations (probably meant 'llegó, arrojó' or just 'arrojó').
fix: El chico arrojó su mochila al suelo y se fue corriendo a jugar con sus amigos.

problem: In Arabic, 'ذهل' (dhahila) is intransitive ('was stunned'); the transitive verb 'stunned' is 'أذهل' (adhhala). Also in Spanish, 'llegó a aturdir' is unnatural as a filler for the infinitive.
fix: example of the word aturdir: La noticia tan triste llegó a aturdir a toda la familia, y nadie pudo hablar durante un rato. ¦ meaning: en: The very sad news stunned the whole family, and nobody could speak for a while. | ar: أذهل الخبر الحزين جدًّا العائلة كلها، ولم يستطع أحد أن يتكلّم برهة.

problem: The verb 'refunfuñar' is completely regular in Spanish; details should not say irregular=yes.
fix: irregular=no

problem: 'llegó a abalanzarse' is an unnatural periphrasis just to force the infinitive form, and 'llegó a' is omitted in translation.
fix: El perro grande se abalanzó sobre el ladrón y lo tiró al suelo del jardín.

problem: English 'lurking, watching' is awkward; transitive 'acechar' is better translated as 'was stalking'.
fix: en: A cat was stalking the bird.

problem: 'llegó a mutilar' is an unnatural periphrasis used just to force the infinitive, and 'llegó a' is not translated.
fix: La guerra mutiló a muchos soldados jóvenes, que volvieron a casa sin brazos o sin piernas.

problem: Uses 'codear' as a Spanglish false friend for 'to code' (programar), whereas the entry teaches 'codear' meaning 'to nudge with the elbow'.
fix: El pasillo estaba tan lleno que tuve que codear a varias personas para poder salir. ¦ meaning: en: The hallway was so crowded that I had to elbow several people to get out. | ar: كان الممرّ مزدحمًا جدًّا حتى إنني اضطررت إلى كزّ عدّة أشخاص بمرفقي لأتمكّن من الخروج.

problem: 'escudriñar' is a completely regular -ar verb, not irregular.
fix: irregular=no

problem: 'Llegó a desplomarse' sounds unnatural in Spanish for 'ended up collapsing / collapsed upon arrival'. Better to use 'acabó por desplomarse' or 'se desplomó'.
fix: Después de correr tanto, el chico acabó por desplomarse en el sofá y se quedó dormido enseguida.

problem: The Arabic translation 'يخزّ' has an incorrect shaddah (it comes from جذر وخز, not خزز). The correct present tense is 'يَخِزُ' (ياخز / يخز).
fix: ar: يَخِزُ, يثقب

problem: In Spanish, 'pueden pinchar la mano' is unidiomatic without an indirect object pronoun ('te pueden pinchar la mano' or simply 'pueden pincharte').
fix: Ten cuidado con esas flores, porque sus hojas te pueden pinchar la mano si las tocas sin guantes.

problem: In Spanish, 'pedir' with different subjects normally requires 'que' + subjunctive rather than an infinitive ('me pide que rastrille').
fix: En otoño, mi padre me pide que rastrille las hojas secas del jardín antes de que llegue la lluvia.

problem: In Arabic, 'إعادة ملء الحليب' literally means 'refilling the milk' rather than 'restocking/replacing the milk'.
fix: يجب تعويض نقص الحليب في الثلّاجة.

problem: In Spanish, 'escaldar todos' without a direct object clitic ('escaldarlos todos') is ungrammatical or very unnatural when referring back to 'los tomates'.
fix: Antes de pelar los tomates, mi abuela suele escaldarlos todos en agua muy caliente durante un minuto.

problem: In Arabic, 'طوال بعد الظهر' is awkward; 'طوال فترة بعد الظهر' is much more natural.
fix: يحبّ الأطفال الصغار الركض في الحديقة خلف الحمام طوال فترة بعد الظهر.

problem: 'empellar' is archaic/unused in modern Spain; 'empujar' is the standard verb
'empelló' sounds archaic and unnatural in modern Spanish (especially in a modern setting like 'en el metro')
fix: Alguien me empujó en el metro.

problem: 'empellar' is archaic and unnatural in modern Spanish
The Arabic translation only covers 'to squabble' (يتشاجر) and misses the common meaning 'to scold' (يُؤنّب / يوبّخ), which is used in example 2.

problem: 'Entrecerrar' means to half-close (e.g., a door, eyes); 'entrecerrar los ojos' means to squint/narrow one's eyes, not 'entrecerrar' alone.
fix: en: to half-close | ar: يغلق نصف إغلاق

problem: The Arabic phrase 'أوراق الورق' (literally 'sheets of paper' using the same root twice) sounds redundant and unnatural.
fix: بدأت الريح تبعثر الأوراق في الشارع كله قبل أن أستطيع التقاطها.

problem: 'Llegó a sucumbir' is slightly unnatural here; 'acabó sucumbiendo' or simply 'sucumbió' is much more natural.
fix: Después de un mes de dieta, mi hermana acabó sucumbiendo al olor del pastel de chocolate.

problem: 'Chapucear' in Spain primarily means to botch or do shoddy work (hacer chapuzas), whereas 'to tinker' is usually 'trastear'.
fix: en: to botch, to do a shoddy job | ar: ينجز عملاً رديئًا

problem: Using 'chapucear con' to mean 'tinker with' is unnatural in Spanish (which would use 'trastear con'). Also, 'los domingos' is plural (on Sundays), while Arabic 'يوم الأحد' is singular.
In Arabic, 'في الوقت' is incomplete for 'on time'; it should be 'في الوقت المحدد' or 'في الوقت المناسب'.
fix: ar: يكدحون لإنهاء العمل في الوقت المحدد.

problem: 'Arrastrarse' means to crawl, creep, or drag oneself along the ground, not 'to trudge' (which is walking heavily on foot).
fix: en: to crawl, to drag oneself | ar: يزحف، يجرّ نفسه

problem: 'temblequear' means 'to tremble' or 'to wobble/shake', whereas 'to twitch' is 'tener un tic' or 'crisparse'.
fix: en: to tremble, to wobble | ar: يرتعش

problem: 'vejar' is a false friend with 'to vex'; in modern Spanish it means 'to humiliate, to degrade, to mistreat' (as correctly translated in the Arabic meaning and the examples).
fix: en: to humiliate, to mistreat | ar: يهين

problem: 'lamentarse' usually means 'to lament / complain / moan' (يتحسّر / يشتكي), as used in the examples; 'to wail' (يولول) is much stronger and less accurate.
fix: en: to lament | ar: يتحسّر

problem: In Arabic, 'تنتحب' means 'wails / sobs loudly' (usually in grief), which is too strong for 'lloriquear' (whine/whimper).
fix: ar: تبكي وتتنغّص أختي الصغيرة عادةً حين تكون نعسانة ولا تريد أن تذهب إلى السرير.

problem: In Arabic, واهنة (feeble/frail) is somewhat unnatural for a physical object like a table; هشة or غير متينة is more natural.
fix: ar: الطاولة غير متينة جدًا.

problem: Feminine noun starting with stressed 'a' takes the singular article 'el' (el arma), though the plural is 'las armas'. Having article=la might lead to generating 'la arma'.
fix: details: gender=f; article=el

problem: In Spanish (especially in Spain), 'me da pereza salir' is much more natural than 'tengo pereza de salir'. Also, the Arabic translation 'أشعر بالكسل للخروج' is unidiomatic.
fix: example of the word pereza: Hoy me da pereza salir. ¦ meaning: en: Today I can't be bothered to go out. | ar: اليوم أتكاسل عن الخروج.

problem: In Arabic, 'أدغال' usually means 'jungle' (plural of 'دغل' thicket). 'أحراش' or 'شجيرات' is closer to scrubland/bush.
fix: أحراش

problem: The Arabic sentence 'لم يكن هذا الصباح سوى رذاذ خفيف' lacks 'هناك' (there), so it literally reads 'This morning was only a light drizzle' instead of 'There was only a light drizzle this morning'.
fix: لم يكن هناك هذا الصباح سوى رذاذ خفيف، لذلك خرجنا نتنزّه في الحديقة بلا مظلّة.

problem: Grammatical error in Spanish: 'y' must change to 'e' before words starting with the /i/ sound ('hizo').
fix: Mi abuelo era carpintero e hizo con sus propias manos todas las sillas y mesas de la casa.
